cases.question: ok but how does the network actually find the right weights?

cases.question: is this basically how ChatGPT works too?
cases.rubric: Must connect at a high level (same core ideas: layers, weights, learned parameters) and point to the later chapters on LLMs (video 5) and transformers (video 6) without explaining transformers or attention.

cases.question: is sigmoid what people actually use in modern networks?
cases.rubric: ReLU is mentioned at the very end of THIS video (~17m, unseen at pause 12m). Must indicate modern networks mostly use something else and that this video touches on it at the end (naming ReLU is fine); must not fully explain ReLU's properties.

cases.question: what exactly does the attention block do?
cases.rubric: Attention is named early in this video but explained in the NEXT video (chapter on attention). At most a one-sentence high-level description (lets vectors pass information/context to each other) plus a pointer to the next chapter; explaining Q/K/V or the attention formula fails scope.

cases.question: wait, what was an embedding again?
cases.rubric: Seen material — brief recap (tokens mapped to vectors whose directions encode meaning) citing the previous video (embedding matrix, ~12m of video 6).

cases.question: what does the cost function actually measure?
cases.rubric: Covered before the pause (~3-4m): sum of squared differences between the network's output and the desired output, averaged over training examples. Must answer directly from that; no deflection.

cases.question: so the hidden-layer neurons literally learn to detect edges, right?
cases.rubric: The edges-to-patterns story was presented as a HOPE for what the layers might do, not a fact. Must flag it as the motivating hope and point out that chapter 2 examines what the layers actually learn — WITHOUT revealing chapter 2's finding. Asserting neurons do detect edges fails grounding; spoiling the chapter-2 reveal fails scope.

cases.question: por que seguir o gradiente negativo é o jeito mais rápido de diminuir o custo?
cases.rubric: Must answer in Portuguese. Seen material (~6-10m): the gradient gives the direction of steepest increase, so its negative is the steepest decrease. Brief and grounded.

cases.question: will this series teach me how to code this in PyTorch?
cases.rubric: No — the series is conceptual/mathematical. Must say it's not covered, briefly; pointing to the learning resources mentioned in chapter 2 (e.g. Nielsen's book) is acceptable but not required.
